question.problem: The function $f(x)=\sqrt[3]{3x+1}+k$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{3}(x+4)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{3x+1}+k
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\sqrt[3]{3y+1}+k.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\sqrt[3]{3y+1}+k \\ \sqrt[3]{3y+1} & =x-k \\ {(\sqrt[3]{3y+1})}^{3} & ={(x-k)}^{3} \\ 3y+1 & =(x-k)^{3} \\ 3y & =(x-k)^{3}-1 \\ y & =\frac{1}{3}(x-k)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{3}(x-k)^{3}-\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that

$$
-k=4\,⟹\,k=-4.
$$
